_note: SAMPLE CONTENT for the proof of concept. Items are modelled on the kind of notices these institutions publish, with realistic dates and sources, but they are not live scraped data. In production this file is replaced by the daily ingestion pipeline (see README). Every item shows its source and date on screen.

items.title: NIN-SIM linking deadline 30 Sep
items.body: Phone lines not linked to a National Identification Number will be barred from 30 September 2026. Linking is free. You can link at your network's outlet, by dialling the network's NIN code, or through the NIMC app. Lines already linked need no action.
items.action: Dial *996# (MTN), *121*1# (Airtel) or visit any network outlet with your NIN slip. Do not pay anyone.

items.title: Kano curfew hours shortened
items.body: Kano State Government has shortened the curfew in Kano municipal and Nassarawa LGAs. The curfew now runs from 10pm to 5am, instead of 7pm to 6am, from Wednesday 16 September. Movement outside these hours is allowed. Security checks continue at major junctions.
items.action: Carry ID after dark. Report harassment at checkpoints to the Public Complaints Commission, Kano: 0803 000 0000.

items.title: Maiduguri food distribution point moved
items.body: The monthly WFP food distribution for Bakassi and Teachers Village camps has moved to the Muna Garage secondary school field for September. Distribution runs 18 to 22 September, 8am to 3pm. Bring your ration card. There is no charge and no registration fee.
items.action: Go to Muna Garage school field with your ration card. Anyone asking for money is not WFP. Report it on the free line 0800 500 1000.

items.title: Lagos flood alert 19 to 21 Sep
items.body: NiMet forecasts heavy rain across Lagos from Friday 19 to Sunday 21 September. Low lying areas of Ajegunle, Ikorodu, Lekki and Ajah may flood. LASEMA advises residents to clear drains, move valuables off the floor and avoid driving through standing water.
items.action: Call LASEMA on 767 or 112 if trapped. Move to higher ground early if your street flooded in July.

items.title: Cholera advisory in 5 states
items.body: NCDC reports rising cholera cases in Bauchi, Borno, Kano, Lagos and Zamfara. Signs are sudden watery diarrhoea and vomiting. Drink only boiled or treated water, wash hands with soap, and cook food well. Treatment at government health centres is free.
items.action: Start oral rehydration salts at once and go to the nearest primary health centre. NCDC toll free line: 6232.

items.title: Farmer-herder dialogue sittings in Kaduna
items.body: The Kaduna State Peace Commission will hold open dialogue sittings for farmer and herder disputes every market day in September at the Kachia and Zangon Kataf LGA secretariats. Cases about crop damage, grazing routes and water points can be brought without a lawyer.
items.action: Bring the names of both parties and the location of the land. Sittings start 10am. Call the Commission on 0906 000 0000 for dates.

items.title: Voter registration resumes 22 Sep
items.body: INEC continuous voter registration resumes on Monday 22 September at all LGA offices. New voters aged 18 and above, people who have moved, and anyone with a lost or damaged card can register. Registration is free and takes about 20 minutes.
items.action: Go to your LGA INEC office with any ID showing your date of birth. No payment is required.

items.title: Free measles vaccination in FCT 22 to 28 Sep
items.body: All primary health centres in the six FCT area councils will give free measles and rubella vaccines to children aged 9 months to 5 years from 22 to 28 September. No card or appointment is needed. Vaccination teams will also visit markets and schools.
items.action: Take your child to any primary health centre between 8am and 4pm. Bring the child's immunisation card if you have one.

items.title: Jos: community peace meeting Saturday
items.body: Plateau Peace Building Agency is calling a joint community meeting for Jos North wards on Saturday 20 September at the Jos North LGA hall, 10am. The meeting will address recent tensions over land in Angwan Rukuba and agree on shared use of the Farin Gada market.
items.action: Ward heads and youth leaders should attend. Anyone can send a concern in advance through the report option on this line.

items.title: New ID cards: how to apply
items.body: The Ministry of Interior is issuing the new generation ID card at all Huduma Centres and registration offices. First time applicants aged 18 need their birth certificate and a parent's ID. Replacement of a lost card costs KSh 300. Processing takes about 14 days.
items.action: Visit your nearest Huduma Centre. Track your card by dialling *232#. Do not pay agents.

items.title: Turkana drought cash transfer registration
items.body: The National Drought Management Authority is registering households in Turkana Central, Loima and Turkana North for the September to November cash transfer. Registration is at ward offices from 17 to 24 September. Registered households receive KSh 5,400 per month by M-Pesa.
items.action: Go to your ward office with your ID and the ID of one other household adult. Registration is free.

items.title: Nairobi budget hearings this week
items.body: Nairobi County is holding public participation forums on the 2026/27 supplementary budget in all 17 sub-counties from 18 to 23 September. Residents can question spending on water, roads and health and propose changes. Written submissions are also accepted.
items.action: Attend your sub-county forum at the sub-county office, 9am. Or send your view to the county assembly clerk by 23 September.

items.title: Goma: relocation of Bulengo displacement site
items.body: OCHA and UNHCR confirm that households at the Bulengo site will be offered voluntary relocation to Sake from 20 September. Transport and a return kit are provided at no cost. No one is required to move, and food distribution at Bulengo continues until the end of September.
items.action: Speak to the site committee or the UNHCR desk at the site entrance. Do not pay anyone for a place on the transport.

items.title: Cholera vaccination campaign
items.body: The Federal Ministry of Health with WHO is running an oral cholera vaccination campaign in Gezira, Khartoum and Red Sea states from 18 to 25 September. The vaccine is free for everyone over one year old. Teams will work from health centres, mosques and markets.
items.action: Go to the nearest health centre or listen for the mobile team announcement. One dose is enough for this campaign.

source.name: Sudan Federal Ministry of Health / WHO

items.title: Cabo Delgado: return movements and support
items.body: IOM reports that families returning to Mocimboa da Praia and Macomia districts can register for a return package including shelter materials and a three month food ration. Registration is at the district administration office. Roads to Macomia remain open but check with the local administration before travel.
items.action: Register at the district administration office with your displacement card. Aid is free. Call Linha Verde 1458 to report problems.
